claims.text: Burke-Gilman Trail had 59 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.0 million a year.
12% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck pedalcyclist, front end at angle” crashes, against 3% at the city's worst crash locations.
5% of crashes here were recorded as “head on” crashes, against 1% at the city's worst crash locations.
3% of crashes here were recorded as “from opposite direction - both moving - head-on” crashes, against 0% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 1.4 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $480,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Burke-Gilman Trail (no road-owner dataset registered for this city, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
